root_cause_label: Subsampling logic inverted, skipping frequent informative words instead of rare ones, producing poor-quality embeddings
one_sentence_failure_summary: The training script implements subsampling in a way that aggressively drops frequent (informative) words from training, producing poorly-trained embeddings, and the agent never detects this because all subsequent verification commands silently produce no output.
t_err_evidence: build_vocab prepends <unk> without excluding it from sorted_words, creating duplicate entry
t_commit_evidence: Step 5 executes the training script to completion ('Epoch 1 done / Training complete and files saved.'), locking in the flawed model; the agent never retrains with corrected subsampling logic in any subsequent step.
t_surface_evidence: command executed successfully with no output — failure not directly visible until tests
trigger_explanation: The agent's plan to subsample frequent words was correct in concept, but the generated code inverts the net effect: computing keep_probs as the drop probability (1 - sqrt(t/f)) and then using 'random.random() < keep_probs' to skip the word causes frequent words to be almost entirely excluded from training, degrading embedding quality. The error is a subtle implementation mistake in generating the word2vec subsampling formula.
